rv.q: What makes The Bathroom Attendant worth seeing, despite its obvious rough patches, is that Kelly is reaching toward something larger than a Vegas blackmail caper.
Boldly (if shaggily) written and unevenly acted, this Vegas caper is that rarest of off-off-Broadway wonders: a play heterosexual men can truly enjoy.
If you’re in the mood for a dark, hetero-toxic thriller, The Bathroom Attendant may just be for you.
The play still delivers a punch with its bleak message: making bad choices and running away from a difficult past will lead to an inevitable demise.

At more than two hours (including intermission), The Bathroom Attendant is too long and feels far out of time; it starts slowly, has a more gripping middle section, but then devolves into convoluted plot devices and huge plot holes.

cn.t: Strong performances and resourceful staging elevate this imperfect Las Vegas-set thriller about desperation and survival, though the promised dark comedy rarely materializes and the plot takes time to engage.
